title: Silicon Sample Benchmark — Tier 1 (individual simulation) submission (team team_27)
description: Tier-1 individual-level predictions for the Silicon Sample Benchmark. This is the secondary-1 entry of a matched pair; it differs from our primary entry by exactly one factor, how the multi-item scales are asked. Here every one of the 44 items is asked in its own independent prompt. A synthetic panel of 9,000 respondents is built by raking the post-stratification weights of 9,000 General Social Survey respondents onto the preregistered quota margins, then quota-sampling within each of the 17 conditions, so demographic composition is not a confound of the treatment effects. Each respondent is assigned one condition (500 per intervention, 1,000 in control, one of the three filler texts for each control respondent), is rendered as a fixed-template persona sentence built in code, with no second model, and then answers all 44 raw survey items one item at a time with local open weights. The 6 composite outcomes are built by the benchmark's own scripts/clean.R from the raw items, never in our code. No human outcome data from this study, or from any pilot of it, informed any part of the pipeline.
